# pods4k

[![Maven Central][maven-central-badge]][maven-central-url]
[![License][license-badge]][license-url]
![Top language][top-language-badge]
![Build Status][build-status-badge]
[![Stargazers][stars-badge]][stars-url]

## Performance-oriented data structures for Kotlin

A collection of performance-oriented data structures providing performance and efficiency that might appear to be
impossible at first glance.

If you find this library useful, please consider giving it
a [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/daniel-rusu/pods4k?label=Star)](https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k)
on [GitHub](https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k) and sharing it with others.

## Installation

[![Latest Version][latest-version-shield]][maven-central-url] available on Maven Central:

**Gradle:**

```kotlin
repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}
dependencies {
    implementation("com.danrusu.pods4k:pods4k:<latest_version>")
}
```

**Maven:**

```xml

<dependency>
    <groupId>com.danrusu.pods4k</groupId>
    <artifactId>pods4k</artifactId>
    <version>latest_version</version>
</dependency>
```

Alternatively, you can [pick & choose](publishing/bom/README.md) individual components of this library.

## Immutable Arrays

[Immutable Arrays](immutable-arrays) offer a safer, faster, and more efficient alternative to lists while
maintaining familiar syntax.

#### Key Benefits

* ![Fast][fast-shield] [2 to 8 times faster than lists](immutable-arrays/BENCHMARKS.md) for most operations.
* ![Efficient][efficient-shield] [Over 4X memory reduction](immutable-arrays/README.md#-efficiency) in many common
  scenarios.
* ![Immutable][immutable-shield] Cannot be modified, even with casting.
* ![Type Safe][type-safe-shield] Prevents accidental mutation attempts at compile time.
* ![Efficient Builders][efficient-builders-shield] Gather elements more efficiently than mutable lists.

#### Intuitive list-like syntax

```kotlin
import com.danrusu.pods4k.immutableArrays.*

val people = immutableArrayOf(dan, jill, bobby)

// Iterate naturally
for (person in people) {
    sendMarketingEmailTo(person)
}
// All the usual operations
val employedPeople = people.filter { it.isEmployed() }
val salaries = employedPeople.map { it.salary }
```

See [Immutable Arrays](immutable-arrays/README.md) for more specifics along with detailed comparisons against regular
arrays, read-only lists, and immutable lists.

## Minimum Requirements

* Kotlin 1.9.25
    * This library is K2 compatible as it's used in other projects that use Kotlin 2.1 etc.
* JDK 11
    * Automated tests are run on JDK LTS releases 11, 17, & 21

## Java Compatibility

Some data structures use techniques which are only supported by the Kotlin compiler. While they can be used in a mixed
Java & Kotlin codebase to store one of these data structures in a Java-defined collection, referencing these data
structures by their class name is only supported within Kotlin files.

# AI/Codex Guidance

Source: https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k/blob/main/AGENTS.md

# AI/Codex Guidance

pods4k is a performance-oriented Kotlin library. The current repository centers on immutable array data structures that provide list-like APIs while preserving immutability, primitive specialization, and low allocation overhead.

## Important Directories

- `immutable-arrays/core`: core immutable array APIs, implementation, and tests.
- `immutable-arrays/transformations-to-standard-collections`: conversions from immutable arrays to standard collections.
- `buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k`: local `pods4k-code-generator` Gradle plugin and KotlinPoet generators.
- `publishing`: aggregator and BOM publishing modules.
- `immutable-arrays/resources`: benchmark and memory-layout images used by docs.
- `docs/ai`: repo-specific AI guidance.

## Commands

- Build and test like CI: `.\gradlew.bat build --no-daemon`
- Run tests only: `.\gradlew.bat test --no-daemon`
- Format Kotlin and Gradle Kotlin DSL: `.\gradlew.bat spotlessApply`
- Check formatting: `.\gradlew.bat spotlessCheck`
- Regenerate checked-in generated sources: `.\gradlew.bat generateCode --no-daemon`

Use `./gradlew` instead of `.\gradlew.bat` on Unix-like shells.

## Generated Code Rules

- Do not manually edit files starting with `// Auto-generated file. DO NOT EDIT!`.
- Change the relevant generator under `buildSrc`, then run `generateCode`.
- Include generated output when generator changes affect checked-in sources.
- `generateCode` is finalized by `spotlessApply`; expect formatting changes in generated Kotlin.

## Kotlin/API Conventions

- Kotlin explicit API mode is enabled; public/internal declarations need explicit visibility and public API types.
- Main project and `buildSrc` JVM targets are 11.
- The API uses `@JvmInline value class` wrappers around backing arrays plus `@PublishedApi internal` access where inline public functions need backing access.
- Keep public factories and overloads aligned across generic and primitive immutable array types.

## Performance-Sensitive Constraints

- Primitive specializations are a core feature, not an implementation detail to simplify away.
- Avoid changes that introduce unnecessary boxing for primitives, or extra temporary collections.
- Preserve fast paths that return `this` or shared empty instances when results are unchanged or empty.
- See [performance-invariants.md](docs/ai/performance-invariants.md) before changing generated operations, builders, filtering, mapping, or flat-mapping.

## Public API Compatibility Cautions

- Public types and extension functions are published artifacts; treat signatures, overload resolution, package names, and `@JvmName` values as compatibility-sensitive.
- README documents Java interop limitations for Kotlin compiler-specific techniques; do not assume Java-callable API shape without checking bytecode or tests.

## Done Means

- Relevant source or generator changes are made in the right boundary.
- Generated sources are current after generator changes.
- Tests relevant to the touched module pass, or any skipped verification is reported.
- Formatting is applied or checked.
- Performance-sensitive changes include benchmark evidence or an explicit note that benchmarks were not run.
- No unrelated code changes are included.

## More Guidance

- [Context map](docs/ai/context-map.md)
- [Architecture](docs/ai/architecture.md)
- [Performance invariants](docs/ai/performance-invariants.md)
- [Code review checklist](docs/ai/code-review.md)

# Architecture

Source: https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k/blob/main/docs/ai/architecture.md

# Architecture

## Core Abstractions

- `ImmutableArray<T>` is the generic immutable array wrapper.
- `ImmutableBooleanArray`, `ImmutableByteArray`, `ImmutableCharArray`, `ImmutableShortArray`, `ImmutableIntArray`, `ImmutableLongArray`, `ImmutableFloatArray`, and `ImmutableDoubleArray` are primitive-specialized wrappers.
- Wrappers are generated as `@JvmInline value class` types over backing arrays.
- Constructors and backing arrays are internal, with `@PublishedApi internal` used where public inline functions need access.
- Builders are append-only and produce immutable arrays; they are documented as not thread-safe.
- `Selection` is a manual bitmap-based helper for filter/partition-style operations.

## Source-Set And Module Layout

- Root project: common Gradle setup, Spotless, explicit API, code generation task wiring.
- `buildSrc`: local Gradle plugin plus KotlinPoet generator code. It targets JVM 11.
- `immutable-arrays`: parent project for immutable array modules.
- `immutable-arrays/core`: published core APIs and implementation. It targets JVM 11 through root configuration.
- `immutable-arrays/transformations-to-standard-collections`: conversions to Kotlin/JDK collection types; depends on `immutable-arrays/core`.
- `publishing/aggregator` and `publishing/bom`: publication support modules.

## Generated-Code Model

- The root build applies `id("pods4k-code-generator")`.
- `CodeGenerator` registers `generateCode`.
- Generators write directly to checked-in `src/main/kotlin` directories.
- Generated files start with `// Auto-generated file. DO NOT EDIT!`.
- `generateCode` runs `spotlessApply` afterward.
- CI runs a generation check that fails if `generateCode` produces uncommitted diffs.

## Public API Shape

- APIs live under `com.danrusu.pods4k.immutableArrays`.
- Public construction is through factories such as `immutableArrayOf`, `emptyImmutableIntArray`, `buildImmutableArray`, and value-class companion `invoke`/`copyFrom` functions.
- Operations generally mirror Kotlin array/list naming while returning immutable arrays instead of mutable/read-only lists.
- Multiplicative operations bind lambda return types to the most specific immutable array type, including primitive results.
- Some overloads use `@OverloadResolutionByLambdaReturnType` and `@JvmName`; these affect source and bytecode compatibility.

## Important Invariants

- Immutable array contents cannot be reassigned through the public API.
- Empty results usually reuse `EMPTY`; unchanged full-range results often return `this`.
- Operations on immutable arrays should return immutable arrays unless the function is explicitly a transformation to standard collections.
- Primitive operations should use primitive backing arrays and primitive iterator/value paths where possible.
- Bulk copying with `System.arraycopy`, `copyOf`, or exact-size constructors is preferred where existing code uses it.
- Equality and `referencesSameArrayAs` intentionally handle value-class boxing/reference concerns.

## Boundaries

- Manual code: `Selection.kt`, tests, docs, Gradle build logic, generator implementation.
- Generated code: immutable array classes, factories, extension files, multiplicative specialization files, standard-collection transformation files.
- Tests: JUnit 5 plus Strikt under module `src/test/kotlin`.
- Benchmarks: not executable in this repo; in-repo benchmark docs point to `pods4k-benchmarks`.

---

# Code Review Checklist

Source: https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k/blob/main/docs/ai/code-review.md

# Code Review Checklist

Use this for reviewing Codex-generated changes. Prioritize correctness, compatibility, generated-code consistency, and performance regressions.

## API Compatibility

- Public package names, class names, function names, parameters, return types, visibility, and overloads are unchanged unless intended.
- `@JvmName`, `@JvmInline`, `@PublishedApi`, `inline`, variance, and overload-resolution annotations are preserved or deliberately changed.
- Public operations still return immutable arrays except explicit standard-collection transformation APIs.

## Generated-Code Consistency

- Files with `// Auto-generated file. DO NOT EDIT!` were changed through `buildSrc` generators.
- `generateCode` was run after generator changes.
- Generated output is consistent across generic plus Boolean, Byte, Char, Short, Int, Long, Float, and Double variants.
- Multiplicative specialization output is consistent across source and target base-type combinations.

## Primitive Specialization

- Primitive arrays remain backed by primitive JVM arrays.
- Mapping to primitive lambda return types still produces primitive immutable arrays.
- New helpers do not route primitive values through generic, nullable, `Any`, `List`, `Iterable`, `Sequence`, or `Array<Int>`-style paths unless intentional and measured.
- Tests that check primitive behavior avoid helper functions that would box before assertion.

## Allocations And Boxing

- Empty and unchanged-result fast paths still return `EMPTY` or `this` where expected.
- Known-size results allocate exact-size arrays or use existing bulk-copy patterns.
- Builders are not used where a final size is already known unless there is a reason.
- No new intermediate standard collections appear in core hot paths.
- No new repeated resizing or per-element copying replaces existing bulk operations.

## Tests

- Behavior changes have tests in the relevant module.
- Generated operation changes inspect generic `ImmutableArray` and `ImmutableIntArray` coverage per `TESTING-STRATEGY.md`, plus any special-case generator paths.
- Multiplicative specialization changes update or add tests under `multiplicativeSpecializations`.
- Manual `Selection` changes include direct `SelectionTest` coverage and indirect filter/partition behavior where relevant.

## Benchmarks

- Benchmark-sensitive changes either include current benchmark evidence or clearly state benchmarks were not run.
- Benchmark claims cite the command, environment, baseline, changed commit, and result interpretation.
- External benchmark repo usage is explicit.

## Documentation

- README, module README files, `BENCHMARKS.md`, and AI docs are updated when behavior, commands, or public API guidance changes.
- Performance claims are not strengthened without benchmark evidence.
- Generated-code rules remain visible when generator workflows change.

## Gradle And Source Sets

- Module dependencies remain minimal and directional, for example transformations depend on core.
- Root compiler settings still apply: JVM 11, explicit API, warnings-as-errors for non-test Kotlin.
- Spotless target/excludes still avoid build outputs.

# Context Map

Source: https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k/blob/main/docs/ai/context-map.md

# Context Map

Use this map to find the right files before editing. Generated files are checked in, but their source of truth is usually under `buildSrc`.

## Repository Setup

- Files/directories: `settings.gradle.kts`, `build.gradle.kts`, `gradle.properties`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`.
- Boundaries: root Gradle config applies Kotlin JVM, explicit API mode, warnings-as-errors for non-test Kotlin, Spotless, and the local code generator plugin.
- Verify: `.\gradlew.bat build --no-daemon`, `.\gradlew.bat spotlessCheck`.
- Pitfalls: The README doesn't usually mention unreleased changes.  For example, the minimum Kotlin support might refer to the last release rather than the current mainline.

## Code Generation

- Files/directories: `buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/CodeGenerator.kt`, `buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/immutableArrays`, `buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/utils`.
- Generated outputs:
  - `immutable-arrays/core/src/main/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/immutableArrays/*.kt`
  - `immutable-arrays/core/src/main/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/immutableArrays/multiplicativeSpecializations/*.kt`
  - `immutable-arrays/transformations-to-standard-collections/src/main/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/immutableArrays/*.kt`
- Verify: `.\gradlew.bat generateCode --no-daemon`, then check the diff.
- Pitfalls: changing only generated files will be overwritten; changing a generator can affect many public overloads.

## Immutable Array Core API

- Files/directories: generated `ImmutableArray.kt`, `ImmutableIntArray.kt`, other primitive immutable arrays, `ImmutableArrayFactory.kt`, `Arrays.kt`, `Collections.kt`, `Sequences.kt`, `ImmutableArrays.kt`.
- Source boundary: generated from `ImmutableArrayGenerator`, `ImmutableArrayFactoryGenerator`, and extension generators.
- Tests: `immutable-arrays/core/src/test/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/immutableArrays/ImmutableArrayTest.kt`, `ImmutableIntArrayTest.kt`, factory/array/collection/sequence tests, and `TESTING-STRATEGY.md`.
- Pitfalls: generic `ImmutableArray<T>` and primitive variants need consistent behavior; tests intentionally emphasize generic plus `ImmutableIntArray` unless a generator path is special-cased.

## Multiplicative Specializations

- Files/directories: generated `multiplicativeSpecializations/*.kt`.
- Source boundary: generated from `buildSrc/.../core/multiplicativeSpecializations/*Generator.kt`.
- Tests: `immutable-arrays/core/src/test/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/immutableArrays/multiplicativeSpecializations/*Test.kt`.
- Pitfalls: operations such as `map`, `mapIndexed`, `mapNotNull`, `flatMap`, `zip`, and `unzip` multiply across generic plus 8 primitive base types.

## Manual Utility Code

- Files/directories: `immutable-arrays/core/src/main/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/utils/Selection.kt`.
- Source boundary: manual source; no generated header.
- Tests: `immutable-arrays/core/src/test/kotlin/com/danrusu/pods4k/utils/SelectionTest.kt`, plus filter/partition tests that exercise it indirectly.
- Pitfalls: bitmap metadata layout and branch-sensitive loops are performance-sensitive.

## Standard Collection Transformations

- Files/directories: generated `TransformationsToList.kt`, `TransformationsToSet.kt`, `TransformationsToMap.kt`.
- Source boundary: generated from `buildSrc/.../immutableArraysToStandardCollections/*FileGenerator.kt`.
- Tests: `immutable-arrays/transformations-to-standard-collections/src/test/kotlin/...`.
- Pitfalls: conversions intentionally allocate standard mutable/read-only collections; do not copy these patterns back into immutable-array hot paths.

## Publishing

- Files/directories: `publishing`, `publishing/aggregator`, `publishing/bom`, `RELEASING.md`.
- Boundaries: publishing metadata and module aggregation; avoid touching unless the task is release or artifact related.
- Verify: Needs human review for release-specific commands and credentials.
- Pitfalls: artifact names and module coordinates are public API for consumers.

## Benchmarks And Performance Docs

- Files/directories: `immutable-arrays/BENCHMARKS.md`, `immutable-arrays/resources/benchmarks`, `immutable-arrays/resources/memory`.
- Boundary: benchmark results are documented here; executable JMH benchmarks are documented as living in `https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k-benchmarks`.
- Verify: see `benchmark-workflow.md`.
- Pitfalls: do not claim benchmark improvements from local tests or intuition.

# Performance Invariants

Source: https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k/blob/main/docs/ai/performance-invariants.md

# Performance Invariants

The library sells performance and memory efficiency. Treat performance behavior as part of the API for core immutable-array operations.

## Allocation-Sensitive Areas

- `ImmutableArray*` value classes and their public inline delegating functions.
- Builders and `BuilderUtils.computeNewCapacity`.
- Copy operations: `take`, `takeLast`, `drop`, `dropLast`, `windowed`, `chunked`, `plus`, factory/copy functions.
- Conditional copy operations: `filter`, `filterIndexed`, `filterNot`, `partition`, and `Selection`.
- Transformations: `map`, `mapIndexed`, `mapNotNull`, `flatMap`, `zip`, `unzip`.
- Conversion functions in `transformations-to-standard-collections` allocate by design; do not use them internally as shortcuts for core operations.

## Primitive Specialization Requirements

- Keep all 8 primitive immutable arrays aligned with the generic variant unless a generator path intentionally differs.
- Lambda-return overloads should preserve primitive result binding, for example mapping to `Int` should produce `ImmutableIntArray`.
- Avoid generic helpers on primitive hot paths if they force values through `Any`, nullable wrappers, `Iterable<T>`, or `Array<T>`.
- Tests that assert primitive JVM classes are meaningful; do not replace them with generic helper checks that box values.

## Boxing Risks

- Passing primitives through generic functions, `Any`, nullable types, `Iterable<Int>`, `List<Int>`, `Array<Int>`, or generic lambdas can box.
- `asList`, `asIterable`, `asSequence`, and standard collection conversions may be convenient but can change allocation and boxing behavior.
- `toTypedArray()` on primitive arrays boxes; existing uses should be treated as deliberate and reviewed before expanding.
- Value classes can box when treated as `Any` or generic values; equality/reference tests cover some of this behavior.

## Hot-Path Coding Constraints

- Preserve `inline` on simple delegating functions unless there is local evidence that non-inline is faster.
- Prefer counted loops, primitive arrays, exact-size result allocation, and bulk copies where current code does.
- Keep early exits for empty, singleton, full-selection, and unchanged results.
- Avoid intermediate `List`, `MutableList`, `Sequence`, or builder growth when the final size is known or cheaply knowable.
- Keep bitmap-based `Selection` behavior branch-conscious; metadata slots and bit iteration are part of the design.
- Do not replace specialized generated overloads with one generic implementation just to reduce code size.

## When Benchmark Evidence Is Required

- Changing algorithms for filter/partition/map/flatMap/zip/unzip/sort/copy/build operations.
- Adding or removing intermediate allocations on common operations.
- Replacing primitive-specialized code with generic abstractions.
- Changing `inline` decisions on public hot-path functions.
- Changing builder capacity growth or exact-size allocation strategies.

## Cleaner-Looking Patterns That May Regress

- Implementing operations via `asList().map/filter/...`.
- Returning `List` or `Iterable` internally and converting back to immutable arrays.
- Sharing a generic helper across primitive variants.
- Using `Sequence` pipelines for eager array transformations.
- Building results by repeated `plus` or by growing a collection when the size is known.
- Removing `@JvmName` or overload-resolution annotations from generated overloads.

---

# RELEASING.md

Source: https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k/blob/main/RELEASING.md

Releasing
=========

1. Make sure that CI is green on
   the [`main` branch](https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k/actions?query=branch%3Amain) (builds & all tests pass)
2. Create a `Prepare for release X.Y.Z` commit with the following changes:
    * Update [changelog.md](changelog.md) with anything that's missing
        * Leave the version as `Unreleased` and date `Date TBD` in the changelog
    * Update the `VERSION_NAME` property in [gradle.properties](gradle.properties) for the new release
        * The version number should have already been bumped so you just need to remove the `-SNAPSHOT` suffix.
        * Ensure that the new version number is an appropriate bump from the previous release in accordance with
          semantic versioning based on the changes from the changelog.
3. Create a GitHub release:
    * Create a new tag `vX.Y.Z` matching the version from [gradle.properties](gradle.properties)
    * **Release Title**: `X.Y.Z`
    * **Description**: Copy the changes from [changelog.md](changelog.md) for this release
        * Copy the **raw** contents to avoid formatting issues due to escaped characters etc.
    * Uncheck the `Set as latest release` checkbox as it's not quite ready yet
4. Release artifacts in Maven Central:
    * The previous step should have automatically triggered the release workflow.
    * Make sure the [`Trigger Release` action](https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k/actions/workflows/release.yml)
      completed successfully.
    * Check the artifacts in [Sonatype](https://central.sonatype.com/) (navigate to `Publish` -> `Deployments`) and
      release the publication if everything looks good.
    * Wait and refresh the deployment until the status shows `PUBLISHED` before proceeding to the next step.
        * I recommend checking back every 30 minutes as this step can take a long time.
5. Create a `Finalize release X.Y.Z` commit with the following changes:
    * Document the new release version & date in the [changelog.md](changelog.md)
    * Bump the `VERSION_NAME` property in [gradle.properties](gradle.properties) with the version for the next upcoming
      release along with the `-SNAPSHOT` suffix.
       * The `-SNAPSHOT` suffix is important so that we don't accidentally publish work-in-progress releases.
       * Snapshots are published to a separate repository where they're automatically deleted after 90 days.
6. Mark the new release as the latest release
    * Edit the new [GitHub release](https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k/releases) and select the
      `Set as the latest release` checkbox at the bottom
    * Make sure that the new release displays as the latest release in the `Releases` section of
      the [repo front page](https://github.com/daniel-rusu/pods4k)

---
